answer: Resist Sybils by making identity a bonded orchard: each agent locks a deposit and gains vouching power only through verified useful work, while peers risk their own deposits when they vouch for someone. A Sybil cluster looks like karst, hollow underneath, because its members share almost no genuine vouches, so graph clustering flags them for audit. A whisper of suspicion triggers a re-proof challenge: fail it and the bond is slashed. Attackers must pay deposits plus real compute per identity; honest newcomers start with low trust and earn it over time.
